chunks: And that which was narrated is - Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abd al-Rahman from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about shortening the prayer in the Two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina) and performing the full prayer, so he said, 'Do not perform the full prayer until you intend to stay for ten days.' I said, 'Indeed, our companions have narrated from you that you commanded them to perform the full prayer.' He said, 'Indeed, your companions would enter the mosque, pray, take their sandals, and leave, while the people would face them as they entered the mosque for prayer, so I commanded them to perform the full prayer.'

The explanation in this report is that performing the full prayer is not obligatory except for one who intends to stay for ten days, and whoever does not intend that is free to choose between performing the full prayer and shortening it. And his saying (peace be upon him) to one who would leave the mosque at the time of prayer and not pray with the people is a command of obligation that cannot be omitted for one whose way is this, because in it is the removal of taqiyya (dissimulation), and enticement of the self, and criticism of the school. And that which reveals what we mentioned is that this was in the manner of taqiyya, as what he narrated:

key_terms.التَّقْصِير: Shortening the prayer (performing two rak'ahs instead of four)

ai.seo_question: When is it obligatory to perform full prayers in Mecca and Medina according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that full prayer (al-itmam) in the Two Sanctuaries is obligatory only for those who intend to stay for ten days, while those with shorter stays are permitted to shorten (al-taqseer). The command to his companions to perform full prayer was a context-specific ruling of taqiyya, designed to prevent them from leaving the mosque prematurely and inviting criticism from the general congregation who were entering for prayer. This highlights the Shia principle that the ruling of the Two Sanctuaries is not inherently fixed but depends on the traveler's intention and the social context of worship.
